current_inference.orientation: Direct manipulation evidence outside Asteraceae supports multiple mechanisms (effective pollination plus abiotic protection) reaching seed/fruit fitness; effect transport to Cirsium remains a hypothesis.
current_inference.stickiness: A universal sticky-is-defence rule is not retained. Direct floral evidence includes strong benefit in Bejaria and a Cirsium null elsewhere in the repository, while whole-plant Datura shows substantial costs; context-dependent defence is the working hypothesis.
current_inference.display: Direct manipulation supports simultaneous pollinator-attraction benefit and seed-predator cost, but broad-angiosperm numerical common-effect extraction is incomplete.
current_inference.bract_defence: Pedicularis rex directly separates pathways: draining water-holding bracts left pollinator visitation unchanged but increased seed predation and reduced final seed set. This supports a defence/protection mechanism rather than generic pollinator attraction.
current_inference.colour_pigmentation: Silene UV exclusion shows that UV exposure induces anthocyanin while depressing pollen and whole-plant seed production. UV is therefore a plausible selection-pressure axis, but this does not demonstrate that darker pigmentation itself increases fitness.
